correctness.rationale: Exact distance classes yield a direct orthogonal decomposition: n(r-1) leaf contrasts have eigenvalue -2^p, n-1 identical 2x2 standard blocks have determinant F_r, and the one-dimensional global zero-sum block has scalar G_{n,r}/(r+1). Strict convexity gives the unique global root. Strict concavity of F_r and h(a)=2*a^alpha-a^2-2 proves that the standard determinant remains positive at that root. The global kernel is one-dimensional; Schoenberg nesting covers all smaller exponents. Independent full shortest-path Gram calculations passed 1180 finite supplementary assertions; the analytic proof covers all n>=3,r>=1. The independent audit has not been performed.

value.rationale: Natural complete two-parameter classification of a sharp Hilbert snowflake invariant of clique coronas; identifies the exact point where a clique with infinite negative-type exponent loses that property after private leaf attachments. The one-dimensional critical load, strict monotonicity and two asymptotic regimes have intrinsic geometric meaning. Most importantly, the known ordinary quadratic embedding constant is unchanged as the core grows although the exact powered-distance threshold deteriorates, proving a mathematically motivated separation of invariants.
